Change c0386. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. III; 1831 Ch. XX.

Context before (unchanged): "Fiend," I exclaimed, "your task is already fulfilled!"

1818 text: I thought of Elizabeth, of my father, and of Clerval; and sunk into a reverie, so despairing and frightful, that even now, when the scene is on the point of closing before me for ever, I shudder to reflect on it.

1831 text: I thought of Elizabeth, of my father, and of Clerval; all left behind, on whom the monster might satisfy his sanguinary and merciless passions. This idea plunged me into a reverie, so despairing and frightful, that even now, when the scene is on the point of closing before me for ever, I shudder to reflect on it.

Diff: I thought of Elizabeth, of my father, and of Clerval; {+all left behind, on whom the monster might satisfy his sanguinary+} and [-sunk-] {+merciless passions. This idea plunged me+} into a reverie, so despairing and frightful, that even now, when the scene is on the point of closing before me for ever, I shudder to reflect on it.

Context after (unchanged): Some hours passed thus; but by degrees, as the sun declined towards the horizon, the wind died away into a gentle breeze, and the sea became free from breakers.

result.rationale: Adds 'all left behind, on whom the monster might satisfy his sanguinary and merciless passions', making the monster's malice toward named family explicit and reframing Victor's reverie as a response to that threat rather than mere despair.
